question: Should host-read capability intentionally accept validated SubRip caption files as a new local-media document type?
rationale: This is a deliberate expansion of a local-file access allowlist, so maintainers must confirm the supported format boundary rather than treating the implementation as a routine MIME-table addition.

options.title: Approve a narrow SubRip boundary
options.body: Require canonical media-core MIME ownership plus redacted after-fix proof of valid `.srt` acceptance and disguised-binary rejection before merge.

options.title: Keep captions outside host-read
options.body: Do not add `.srt` to the host-read allowlist if caption ingestion should remain an explicit future product/security decision.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow SubRip boundary
recommendation.body: Require canonical media-core MIME ownership plus redacted after-fix proof of valid `.srt` acceptance and disguised-binary rejection before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only identified human reviewer who has already evaluated the affected host-read proof requirement.
